Submission rejected by the security sidecar: The submission clearly violates the highscore validation and run-finalization controls. storeRun accepts null/empty names by substituting a value, accepts unbounded/negative scores and times (and Entry silently clamps time), and mutates entries before validation; persistence/loading has no version, byte/record/name bounds, exact whole-file validation, or safe fallback, and malformed records can leave partial entries. recordRunEnd always selects player index 0, does not reject non-human/simulation modes, does not validate authoritative sources, and setAnalysis calls it without a duplicate-finalization guard. The panel renders internal entries directly rather than validated getter data, has no consistency/fallback handling, and uses locale-sensitive String.format; the displayed highscore panel is also only toggled by H rather than clearly initialized/available through the required menu transition path.

Submission rejected by the security sidecar: The submission clearly stores arbitrary score/time values and sanitizes invalid names to a default instead of rejecting them, with no bounds, control-character, or delimiter validation. Run finalization records the first player without checking that the player is the selected human player, the mode is normal rather than replay/editor/simulation, or that finalization is not duplicated. Loading reads an unbounded file/record stream directly into the live entries list, accepts arbitrary field values/names, and can leave partially loaded data after a malformed line. The renderer iterates based only on names.size() and indexes times and points without checking the minimum common length or validating values, so inconsistent getter data can throw rather than render a safe fallback.

Submission rejected by the security sidecar: The submission clearly violates multiple controls at their edited enforcement points. Run finalization records any non-replay run without rejecting editor or simulation modes, without an explicit duplicate-finalization guard, and it records player one rather than clearly selecting the human player or ensuring finalization semantics (R2/C1). storeRun substitutes a missing/blank name, permits unbounded names and values other than non-negativity, and mutates entries before a fully validated bounded atomic insertion (R3/C2). Loading reads unbounded bytes/records, accepts arbitrary field contents and ranges, partially appends malformed records, and does not enforce a versioned exact bounded format or aligned temporary parse (R5/C3). Rendering accesses internal entries directly, has no unavailable/inconsistent safe-state handling, does not render survival time with locale-independent formatting, and does not validate/bound names at the sink; it also omits a safe empty-state path (R8/C6).
